reader.requirement: At --std 85 a relation between an index data item and an index-name or another index data item compares their actual (stored) values without conversion, and an index data item is not comparable with any other operand (numeric item, literal, ZERO, alphanumeric).
reader.edition-search: Same greps as the GR2 case over RelationComparability.cs, StatementValidation.CheckGeneralRelationComparability, NumericRenderer.cs and ConditionRenderer.cs: no edition switch on the class-index pair; Breach answers null for li && ri (two class-index operands) and IndexPair otherwise, at every edition.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: pb1468 exercises IDA = I1 (equal and unequal) only; not index-data-item vs index-data-item, the reversed order, index data items set from index-names of tables with different element sizes, a subordinate index data item, ordering operators, or the refusal half

probes.printed: 01 EQ (IDA=I1), 02 EQ (I1=IDA), 03 EQ (IDA=IDB), 04 LT (IDA<I2), 05 LT (NOT <), 06 LT (IDA<IDB), 07 GT, 08 EQ (IDC from J1 of a PIC X table = IDA from I1 of a PIC X(7) table, both occurrence 4), 09 EQ (IDC=J1), 10 LT
probes.expected: 'The actual values are compared without conversion'; the stored value of an index data item is the index-name's value moved by SET without conversion (implementor-defined representation, here the occurrence number)

probes.printed: COBOL2533 at IDA = 1, IDA = N, IDA = ZERO, IDA = XA, N = IDA; exit 65
probes.expected: 'Relation tests may be made only between' ... 'An index data item and an index-name or another index data item': no other partner

citations.check: OK  §1985:VI.6.3.1.1.3 GR3  (6.3.1.1.3 Comparisons Involving Index-Names and/or Index Data Items)  the text is in GR3

reader.notes: Index-names and index data items share one representation (the occurrence number), so 'without conversion' compares the same values the SET moved. Classes a and e do not apply (no variable-length or file reach for an index data item compare); class c: the pairing list is the same in 1985 and later editions.

refuter.evidence: refute-1985-021/idx3.cob --std 85 (idx3-001): group MOVE GA TO GB carrying an index data item, GIB = GIA EQ and GIB = I1 EQ; OCCURS USAGE INDEX elements TIX(1) > TIX(2) GT, TIX(K) = I1 EQ; SET J1 (PIC X table) TO TIX(1) then J1 = TIX(1) EQ (no conversion); CALL BY REFERENCE of a group holding an index data item, callee SET LO TO LI, LO = LI EQ, caller IDA = GIA EQ, IDA = I1 EQ; abbreviated TIX(K) = I1 AND I2 OR TIX(2) F and TIX(2) NOT = I1 AND NOT I2 T (both match hand expansion). idx3r.cob --compile-only: COBOL2533 at IDA = FUNCTION INTEGER(N), IDA = N + 1, IDA = HIGH-VALUES, IDA = FUNCTION REVERSE(X1), IDA = I1 OR 2 (the carried literal 2 opposite IDA); I1 = 1 AND IDA admitted (I1 = IDA is a legal pair). cite: OK  §1985:VI.6.3.1.1.3 GR3 the text is in GR3.
